lines.text: This is CONTINUA. The network changes. The session doesn't.
Two rescue rovers, one island road, four networks. One runs CONTINUA. The other waits for its network to break.
Watch a handoff. The camera flies out to the access point the new link comes from, then rides the beam back to the rover.
Let's slow it down, and switch on coverage, to see where every network reaches.
Now the clever part. CONTINUA carries a road map from earlier drives. Seventy-nine metres before the cutting, it starts satellite, before Wi-Fi and cellular drop out together.
Satellite was already up, so CONTINUA keeps the link. The normal rover is cut off, and has to stop.
Your turn. Press W, and you're driving. A and D steer, S brakes, and the road keeps you on it.
Every network and handoff you see is the recorded run at your exact point on the road. Drive on, it plays forward. Back up, it plays back.
Escape hands it back to autopilot. Details opens every measurement, down to each kind of traffic.
The results: every strategy, the same road, twenty drives each. CONTINUA kept the link every time, at about a third of the cost of keeping every network on.
The decision log shows every choice the controller made, and why.
The brief page maps each of the challenge's success criteria to its evidence, including where prediction didn't pay.
CONTINUA, by Team Kanban. The network changes. The session doesn't.
